gap: No result ChatGPT got states the under-$300 picks on one basis: continuous watts with the boost modes stripped out (the EcoFlow '1,000 W' and BLUETTI '1,500 W' figures are X-Boost and Power Lifting, so every pick is a 300-600 W machine), cycle life with its end-of-life percentage, and the rated lifetime energy each dollar buys (Pecron E500LFP 2,016 kWh for $269; BLUETTI Elite 30 mini 1,728 kWh for $199, with no percentage given by BLUETTI).
standout_why: Compared against Nineteen Lab (the cited page), Portable Power Rank and PowerStationPicks. Nineteen Lab already labels Power Lifting as resistive-only and gives one end-of-life threshold (Jackery 300 v2, 4,000 cycles to 70%), so the boost half of this is partly covered. It gives no cycle count for the EcoFlow or the BLUETTI, no prices, and lists the River 2 Max at 512 Wh, while the unit EcoFlow's US store sells at $289 is the 499 Wh 'RIVER 2 Max 500'. Portable Power Rank has prices but no cycle claims at all, and calls the Elite 30 V2's 1,500 W a 'peak'. PowerStationPicks quotes '4,000+' and '3,000+' cycles with no percentage. None of the three lists the Segway Lumina 500 or the Pecron E500LFP, two of ChatGPT's three picks, and none works out lifetime energy per dollar.
decides: It confirms the capacity-per-dollar order and adds a second ranking. On dollars per rated Wh, the Segway Lumina 500 leads at $0.29/Wh on Amazon ($149.99, lower than the $199.99 Curacao price ChatGPT showed), then Pecron E500LFP $0.47, EcoFlow RIVER 2 Max 500 $0.58, Elite 30 mini $0.69 and Elite 30 V2 $1.01. So the Elite 30 V2 cannot honestly be #1 on capacity; its case is the 10 ms UPS with 980 W bypass, 80% in 45 minutes, about 9.5 lb and a 5-year warranty. On rated lifetime energy per dollar the order flips: the Elite 30 mini (6,000+ cycles) is at about 11.5 cents per kWh, ahead of the Pecron at 13.3 and the EcoFlow at 19.3. That is a segment a linked product wins (longest-lived and lightest, for 300 W loads), with the caveat that BLUETTI's page gives no end-of-life percentage. The Segway's cycle rating could not be sourced, so it has no place in that second ranking.

findings.value: Pecron E500LFP 2,016 kWh, 13.3 cents/kWh (to 80%, maker); EcoFlow RIVER 2 Max 500 1,497 kWh, 19.3 cents/kWh (to 80%, from the 512 Wh model's manual); BLUETTI Elite 30 mini 1,728 kWh, 11.5 cents/kWh (no percentage given); BLUETTI Elite 30 V2 864 kWh, 33.6 cents/kWh (no percentage given)

findings.note: 576x3,500; 499x3,000; 288x6,000; 288x3,000, each divided into the price read. No capacity fade or inverter loss applied, so real delivered energy is lower for all. At one full cycle a day, 3,000 cycles is 8.2 years and 6,000 is 16.4 years, so calendar ageing would cap the mini's advantage for an occasional user. The footnote is the finding: only Pecron states its threshold on its own page.

findings.label: AC recharge times put on the same basis
findings.value: To 80%: BLUETTI Elite 30 V2 45 min, Elite 30 mini 46 min, Pecron E500LFP 60 min. To 100%: EcoFlow RIVER 2 Max 500 60 min, BLUETTI Elite 30 V2 70 min (380 W), Pecron 90 min (500 W), Elite 30 mini 103 min
findings.source_title: Maker pages listed in the findings above
findings.note: EcoFlow states only 0-100%; BLUETTI headlines 80%. Energy added per minute to full: EcoFlow 499 Wh in 60 min (8.3 Wh/min), Pecron 576 Wh in 90 (6.4), Elite 30 V2 288 Wh in 70 (4.1), mini 288 Wh in 103 (2.8). The larger units refill more energy per minute even where the BLUETTI percentages look faster. The 70 min is listed as 'AC Charging: 70 Mins, 380W'; the page does not say outright that it means a full charge.
